title: The sun and the stars do not change their order — against the one who thinks to change times
summary_md: Uriel closes the reckoning of the sun and the moon with a plain statement about what the lights will and will not do: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). The lights keep the order they were given, and Enoch wrote it down so that his children would keep it too. He also saw where the fault would lie when the reckoning went wrong, and it was never with the heavens: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5). Daniel was shown the one who would make a program of that fault, the horn that wars on the saints: *And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.* (Daniel 7:25). To change the times is to fight the Creator's own order, and the Torah had already warned that the lights are servants of the appointed times and never gods, never men's to re-order: *And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them...* (Deuteronomy 4:19). Against all of it stands the blessing Enoch pronounces on those who keep the count as the sun keeps it: *Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days.* (1 Enoch 82:4). The order is covenant, and the sun has never once broken it.
note: All three Enoch quotes were invented; re-formed on 74:12, 82:5 and 82:4, which carry the same thought. Daniel 7:25 and Deuteronomy 4:19 kept verbatim. Title adjusted to the live verse.

title: The leaders set over the seasons — the moedim written into creation
summary_md: Enoch sees an ordered hierarchy of luminary-captains set over every division of time: *And the leaders of the heads of the thousands, who are placed over the whole creation and over all the stars, have also to do with the four intercalary days, being inseparable from their office, according to the reckoning of the year, and these render service on the four days which are not reckoned in the reckoning of the year.* (1 Enoch 75:1). Uriel is set over the whole company of them, *For the signs and the times and the years and the days the angel Uriel showed to me, whom Yahuah (Lord) of glory hath set for ever over all the luminaries of the heaven, in the heaven and in the world, that they should rule on the face of the heaven and be seen on the earth, and be leaders for the day and the night, i.e. the sun, moon, and stars, and all the ministering creatures which make their revolution in all the chariots of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 75:3). This is no invention of Enoch's; it is the Creator's own order from the fourth day, when the lights were set to mark out the times: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14). The feasts of Leviticus 23 are therefore fixed by the luminaries and not declared by men. The Psalmist names the same governance, *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalms 104:19), and earthly Yashar'el (Israel) mirrored the heavenly ranks in the priestly *courses, which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year* (1 Chronicles 27:1). The stars themselves are summoned to bless the One who set them: *He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.* (Psalms 148:6). The appointed times are the Creator's covenant order, and it ain't new.
note: Draft's 75:1 quote stood; the inline '75:2–75:6' phrase-citations (the four parts, the seven days, the months…) were not in the live chapter, so replaced with 75:3 quoted in full. Rest kept.

title: The four intercalary days that complete the 364-day year
summary_md: Here is the heart of the Enoch reckoning, the part of the solar order men most often neglect: *And the leaders of the heads of the thousands, who are placed over the whole creation and over all the stars, have also to do with the four intercalary days, being inseparable from their office, according to the reckoning of the year, and these render service on the four days which are not reckoned in the reckoning of the year.* (1 Enoch 75:1). Enoch says outright that these four days are where the count goes wrong, and where the true year is completed: *And owing to them men go wrong therein, for those luminaries truly render service on the world-stations, one in the first portal, one in the third portal of the heaven, one in the fourth portal, and one in the sixth portal, and the exactness of the year is accomplished through its separate three hundred and sixty-four stations.* (1 Enoch 75:2). Jubilees gives the very same command, with the very same warning that men would drop these days: *And command you the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they observe the years according to this reckoning-three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts; for everything will fall out in them according to their testimony, and they will not leave out any day nor disturb any feasts. But if they do neglect and do not observe them according to His commandment, then they will disturb all their seasons, and the years will be dislodged from this (order), and they will disturb the seasons and the years will be dislodged and they will neglect their ordinances.* (Jubilees 6:32), and the reckoning is written down *lest they forget the feasts of the covenant and walk according to the feasts of the nations* (Jubilees 6:35). The year of three hundred and sixty-four whole days, completed by these four added days, is the Creator's calendar, and to leave them out is to dislodge the feasts. Genesis had already set the lights *for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), and the appointed times of Leviticus 23 hang on that order.
note: Old inline citations 75:11-13 (the four names, '364 days') are not in the live chapter; replaced with 75:2 in full, which carries both the men-go-wrong warning and the 364 stations. Jubilees and Genesis kept verbatim.

title: The sun and the stars complete the year with perfect justice — covenant order in the heavens
summary_md: The reckoning of the heavens ends on the obedience of the lights: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). The sun has an exactness of its own that Enoch is careful to record: *And the year is accurately completed in conformity with their world- stations and the stations of the sun, which rise from the portals through which it (the sun) rises and sets 30 days.* (1 Enoch 74:17). This is the same testimony the book opened with, before a single vision was given: *Observe ye everything that takes place in the heaven, how they do not change their orbits, and the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set in order each in its season, and transgress not against their appointed order.* (1 Enoch 2:1). It is the covenant the prophets appeal to as the surest thing in creation, *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD); If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth;* (Jeremiah 33:25), an ordinance so fixed it cannot be broken: *He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.* (Psalms 148:6). The lights keeping their law is the standing rebuke to men who would change the times. Where the sun never once delays its station, the order it traces out is the Creator's covenant and not a burden laid on anyone, and the heavens keep the reckoning so faithfully that men are called to keep it the same way.
note: 75:15 does not exist in Charles; the thought lives at 74:12 and 74:17 — re-formed there. 2:1, Jeremiah 33:25, Psalm 148:6 kept. Title adjusted to the live wording.

title: Twelve portals at the ends of the earth — the winds in their treasuries
summary_md: Uriel shows Enoch the order at the world's edge: *And at the ends of the earth I saw twelve portals open to all the quarters (of the heaven), from which the winds go forth and blow over the earth.* (1 Enoch 76:1). They are laid out by quarter, not scattered at random: *Three of them are open on the face (i.e. the east) of the heavens, and three in the west, and three on the right (i.e. the south) of the heaven, and three on the left (i.e. the north).* (1 Enoch 76:2). The winds come out of appointed gates by the Creator's reckoning, and the Tanakh confesses the same honest geography: *He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain; he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries* (Psalm 135:7). The wind is kept in a treasury and brought out by Yahuah's (God's) hand, never summoned by men. Job hears the order spoken from the same edge of creation: *By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?* (Job 38:24). The lights of Genesis 1 were set *for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), and the winds keep their stations in the same way, the Creator's covenant order written into the world. Jubilees names the angels set over these powers on the first day: *and the angels of the spirit of the winds, and the angels of the spirit of the clouds, and of darkness, and of snow and of hail and of hoar frost... and the angels of the spirits of cold and of heat* (Jubilees 2:2). The gates, the treasuries and the appointed winds are one order under one Maker.
note: The 76:1 quote was a blend of 36:1 and 76:1; replaced with the live 76:1 and 76:2 in full. Canon and Jubilees witnesses kept verbatim.

title: Winds of blessing and prosperity, winds of desolation and drought
summary_md: The twelve portals are not all alike, and Enoch is told plainly which are which: *Through four of these come winds of blessing and prosperity, and from those eight come hurtful winds: when they are sent, they bring destruction on all the earth and on the water upon it, and on all who dwell thereon, and on everything which is in the water and on the land.* (1 Enoch 76:4). The first of them is named with its charge, *And the first wind from those portals, called the east wind, comes forth through the first portal which is in the east, inclining towards the south: from it come forth desolation, drought, heat, and destruction.* (1 Enoch 76:5), and the middle gate beside it carries the opposite: *And through the second portal in the middle comes what is fitting, and from it there come rain and fruitfulness and prosperity and dew; and through the third portal which lies toward the north come cold and drought.* (1 Enoch 76:6). So the winds are sorted to blessing and to hurt, dew and rain on one hand and drought and desolation on the other, which are exactly the two roads the covenant sets before a people. Job knows this sorting by quarter too: *Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north* (Job 37:9). The directions are not neutral; they are assigned. The whole order stands under one Maker, and the withholding of rain is never arbitrary but follows a broken covenant, while the dew and the rain are the blessing-wind brought out of His treasuries. Enoch is shown the whole catalogue so the reckoning can be kept, not so men might control the sky.
note: Both Enoch quotes were off (76:4 reworded, 76:5 invented); re-formed on the live 76:4, 76:5 and 76:6. Job 37:9 kept.

title: The twelve completed — the four winds from the four quarters
summary_md: Uriel closes the survey: *And the twelve portals of the four quarters of the heaven are therewith completed, and all their laws and all their plagues and all their benefactions have I shown to thee, my son Methuselah.* (1 Enoch 76:14). Twelve gates resolve into the four cardinal quarters, and each wind bears its law, its plague, and its benefaction. The prophets reckon by these same four quarters when Yahuah (God) moves in judgment: *And upon Elam will I bring the four winds from the four quarters of heaven, and will scatter them toward all those winds* (Jeremiah 49:36). Daniel's vision opens on the same fourfold order stirred over the deep: *I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea* (Daniel 7:2). The winds out of which the beast-kingdoms rise are the very ordered powers Enoch catalogues. They keep their stations under the Creator; their laws and their plagues alike are His to send, and reading the order rightly is part of keeping the covenant reckoning.
note: Draft's live 76:14 quote already fit the prose (it speaks of portals and laws/plagues/benefactions); only light smoothing of the connecting sentences.

title: The garden of righteousness in the north — the tree of wisdom
summary_md: When Enoch names the four quarters he places the garden in the north: *And the fourth quarter, named the north, is divided into three parts: the first of them is for the dwelling of men: and the second contains seas of water, and the abysses and forests and rivers, and darkness and clouds; and the third part contains the garden of righteousness.* (1 Enoch 77:3). He had already walked in it on an earlier journey and seen the tree that stands there: *That tree is in height like the fir, and its leaves are like (those of) the Carob tree: and its fruit is like the clusters of the vine, very beautiful: and the fragrance of the tree penetrates afar.* (1 Enoch 32:4). This is Eden's own garden: *And out of the ground made Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.* (Genesis 2:9). The garden of righteousness is not lost forever. The tree of life stands again in the restored city, *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2), and Ezekiel saw it lining the river from the sanctuary: *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). Enoch's garden in the north is the canon's Eden, lost and restored.
note: 77:7 'paradise of righteousness... tree of wisdom' is invented; the live 77:3 carries the garden of righteousness in the north. 32:4 (already re-quoted from the live text) kept; Genesis 3:7 dropped since the 'eyes opened' phrase it answered is gone. Title adjusted.

title: The prison of the stars that did not come forth at their appointed times
summary_md: Past the abyss Enoch sees a waste place that has become a prison for the host of heaven: *I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, The angel said: ‘This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:13-14). The charge against them is precise, and it is a calendar charge: *And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (Lord) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.* (1 Enoch 18:15). They broke the appointed times that were set into the lights on the fourth day: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14). Enoch is shown the same prisoners a second time, and Uriel gives the same reason: *These are of the number of the stars of heaven, which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (Lord), and are bound here till ten thousand years, the time entailed by their sins, are consummated.’* (1 Enoch 21:6). The apostles carry the same bound and reserved host forward, *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;* (2 Peter 2:4), and Jude names them as the lawless lights: *Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.* (Jude 1:13). These are the same lights men are warned never to worship as gods: *And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.* (Deuteronomy 4:19). The reckoning is the Creator's covenant, and Jubilees commands the very order whose neglect disturbs every feast: *And command you the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they observe the years according to this reckoning-three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts...* (Jubilees 6:32). The stars in prison are what a perverted calendar looks like from heaven's side; the right reckoning is faithfulness, and it ain't new.
note: The old 77:10-11 addresses do not exist; the words live at 18:13-15 and 21:6. Removed the duplicated 18:15 quote the mechanical pass produced and put 21:6 in its place. Canon witnesses kept.

title: The names of the sun and moon — the two great lights
summary_md: Enoch gives the luminaries their names: *And the names of the sun are the following: the first Orjârês, and the second Tômâs.* (1 Enoch 78:1), *And the moon has four names: the first name is Asônjâ, the second Eblâ, the third Benâsê, and the fourth Erâe.* (1 Enoch 78:2), and then he says what they are together: *These are the two great luminaries: their circumference is like the circumference of the heaven, and the size of the circumference of both is alike.* (1 Enoch 78:3). This is creation week itself: *And Elohim (God) made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also* (Genesis 1:16). The naming is not an idle catalogue. It is the order the heavens keep, so that they can sing it back to the One who set them: *Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light* (Psalm 148:3), for *he commanded, and they were created* (Psalm 148:5). The lights belong to the Creator and carry His reckoning; they are servants set in their stations, never powers to be feared or worshipped.
note: Both Enoch quotes were invented; re-formed on the live 78:1-3, which carry the names and 'the two great luminaries'. Canon kept.

title: The 364-day solar reckoning — the moon falls behind
summary_md: Enoch sets the sun as the measure of the year, and he is exact about it: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). The moon does not keep that pace. Her year is counted in two halves of one hundred and seventy-seven days, *And three months she makes of thirty days, and at her time she makes three months of twenty-nine days each, in which she accomplishes her waning in the first period of time, and in the first portal for one hundred and seventy-seven days.* (1 Enoch 78:15), and Uriel adds up what that costs her against the sun: *And the overplus of the sun and of the stars amounts to six days: in 5 years 6 days every year come to 30 days: and the moon falls behind the sun and stars to the number of 30 days.* (1 Enoch 74:11). That gap is the whole point. The lunar count runs behind the solar order, so the reckoning is fixed by the sun. Jubilees lays the same charge on Yashar'el (Israel): *command you the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they observe the years according to this reckoning-three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts* (Jubilees 6:32). The year of three hundred and sixty-four whole days is the Creator's calendar, set on the fourth day, and the appointed times stand or fall by it. Keeping that reckoning is covenant faithfulness and not a later invention of men.
note: The old 78:4-5 and 74:10,13 quotes were invented; the live 74:12, 74:11 and 78:15 carry the 364-day sun and the moon falling behind. Jubilees kept.

title: Her light waxes and wanes — the new moon appointed for worship
summary_md: Enoch measures the moon's fullness part by part: *And when the moon rises one-fourteenth part appears in the heaven: [the light becomes full in her]: on the fourteenth day she accomplishes her light.* (1 Enoch 78:6), and he names the first day of the count: *And on the first day she is called the new moon, for on that day the light rises upon her.* (1 Enoch 78:12). The waxing and the waning are not chaos; they are appointment, and the moon is set for the times Yashar'el (Israel) keeps. So the Psalm fixes the trumpet to her renewal, *Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day* (Psalm 81:3), and the prophet sees worship itself ordered by that cycle: *it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 66:23). The phases Enoch reckons are the Creator's clock for the appointed times. The new moon is written into the light itself, and keeping it is covenant worship.
note: 78:6 was invented; the live 78:6 and 78:12 carry the waxing count and the naming of the new moon. Psalm 81:3 and Isaiah 66:23 kept.

title: The law of the moon's light — set for signs and seasons
summary_md: Uriel does not leave the moon's course to guesswork; he gives Enoch its law: *And Uriel showed me another law: when light is transferred to the moon, and on which side it is transferred to her by the sun.* (1 Enoch 78:10), and he fixes the day the count begins: *And on the first day she is called the new moon, for on that day the light rises upon her.* (1 Enoch 78:12). The whole reckoning was handed down for the festivals and not for curiosity: *And the account thereof is accurate and the recorded reckoning thereof exact; for the luminaries, and months and festivals, and years and days, has Uriel shown and revealed to me, to whom Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the world hath subjected the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 82:7). This is the fourth-day charge spoken back: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), where the seasons are the appointed times. The Psalm seals it, *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down* (Psalm 104:19), and the heavens preach their Maker's order: *The heavens declare the glory of Elohim (God); and the firmament sheweth his handywork* (Psalm 19:1). The lights keep their law, and men are called to keep the reckoning they mark. To neglect or change that order is the work of the one who would *think to change times and laws* (Daniel 7:25), but the Creator's calendar stands, fixed in the lights.
note: The 78:9,11,12 quotes were invented; re-formed on the live 78:10, 78:12 and 82:7 (which names luminaries, months and festivals together). Canon kept. Title adjusted.

title: The law of all the stars completed — the luminaries set for the appointed times
summary_md: Uriel's survey of the heavens ends with a word to Methuselah that the whole thing is law: *And now, my son, I have shown thee everything, and the law of all the stars of the heaven is completed.* (1 Enoch 79:1). What was shown covers every measure of time a people needs to keep the feasts: *And he showed me all the laws of these for every day, and for every season of bearing rule, and for every year, and for its going forth, and for the order prescribed to it every month and every week:* (1 Enoch 79:2). The appointed times were never invented by men. They were written into creation by the lights on the fourth day: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14). The same order is sung in the Psalm, *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19), and it is the very fabric the prophet swears by: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name:* (Jeremiah 31:35). The calendar is the Creator's covenant order, and the appointed times stand because the lights stand.
note: 79:3 quote was invented; re-formed on the live 79:1-2. Canon kept. 'It ain't new' dropped from the title since the live verse carries the thought plainly.

title: Every luminary in its order — the host of heaven serve their Maker
summary_md: Enoch signs off the luminaries with the name of the one who showed them to him: *Such is the picture and sketch of every luminary which Uriel the archangel, who is their leader, showed unto me.* (1 Enoch 79:6). The lights are obedient servants under a leader, never powers of their own, and Uriel had already told Enoch how exactly they keep their station: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). They do not stray because *He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.* (Psalm 148:6), the very heavens commanded to *Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light.* (Psalm 148:3). Their silent obedience preaches: *The heavens declare the glory of Elohim (God); and the firmament sheweth his handywork.* (Psalm 19:1). And because they keep their order, they become the surety of the covenant itself: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD); If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth;* (Jeremiah 33:25). The hosts serve their Maker, which is exactly why the Torah forbids serving them: *And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.* (Deuteronomy 4:19).
note: 79:4 quote was invented; re-formed on the live 79:6 and 74:12. Canon kept. Title adjusted.

title: The 364-day solar order and the moon falling behind
summary_md: Enoch fixes the primary reckoning by the sun: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). The moon is measured against that and comes up short. Her half-year is counted out, *And the waning which takes place in the first portal in its season, till one hundred and seventy-seven days are accomplished: reckoned according to weeks, twenty-five (weeks) and two days.* (1 Enoch 79:4), and then the lag is named: *She falls behind the sun and the order of the stars exactly five days in the course of one period, and when this place which thou seest has been traversed.* (1 Enoch 79:5). Uriel had already summed the same shortfall over the years: *And the overplus of the sun and of the stars amounts to six days: in 5 years 6 days every year come to 30 days: and the moon falls behind the sun and stars to the number of 30 days.* (1 Enoch 74:11). So the solar order is the measure and the lunar year lags behind it. Jubilees commands the same three hundred and sixty-four days, with the same diagnosis of the moon: *And command you the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they observe the years according to this reckoning-three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts; for everything will fall out in them according to their testimony, and they will not leave out any day nor disturb any feasts.* (Jubilees 6:32), and the very lag Enoch names: *For there will be those who will assuredly make observations of the moon–now (it) disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon.* (Jubilees 6:36). The whole-day solar order completes the year in righteousness, and it ain't new.
note: All three Enoch quotes were invented; re-formed on the live 74:12, 79:4-5 and 74:11, which carry the 364 days and the moon's lag. Jubilees kept.

title: Preserve the books and keep the reckoning — blessed are those who walk in it
summary_md: The law of the luminaries is handed down to be kept, not catalogued. Enoch gives it to his son with a charge: *And now, my son Methuselah, all these things I am recounting to thee and writing down for thee, and I have revealed to thee everything, and given thee books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from thy father’s hand, and (see) that thou deliver them to the generations of the world.* (1 Enoch 82:1), and he says what it is for: *I have given wisdom to thee and to thy children, [And thy children that shall be to thee], That they may give it to their children for generations, This wisdom (namely) that passeth their thought.* (1 Enoch 82:2). The blessing is on those who keep the count as the sun keeps it: *Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days.* (1 Enoch 82:4). The feasts those years carry are the appointed times the Torah fixes: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.* (Leviticus 23:2). When men refuse the order, Daniel shows whose work that is: *And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.* (Daniel 7:25). To keep the right reckoning is covenant faithfulness; to change the times is rebellion against the Creator's order.
note: 79:8-10 do not exist and 82:5 was misquoted; re-formed on the live 82:1, 82:2 and 82:4. Leviticus 23:2 and Daniel 7:25 kept. Title adjusted.

title: They shall err and take them to be gods — the host of heaven
summary_md: Uriel tells Enoch what happens to the luminaries in the days of the sinners: *And the moon shall alter her order, And not appear at her time.* (1 Enoch 80:4), and the stars with her: *And many chiefs of the stars shall transgress the order (prescribed). And these shall alter their orbits and tasks, And not appear at the seasons prescribed to them.* (1 Enoch 80:6). When the lights no longer keep their appointed reckoning, men do not return to the Creator who set them. Uriel says exactly where it ends: *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). That is the very snare Moses warned against on the plains of Moab: *And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.* (Deuteronomy 4:19). Jeremiah names the same apostasy when the bones of the idolaters are spread out before the very host they served: *And they shall spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served, and after whom they have walked, and whom they have sought, and whom they have worshipped...* (Jeremiah 8:2). Paul names the root of it, the creature exalted over the Creator: *Who changed the truth of Elohim (God) into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.* (Romans 1:25). The sun and moon are servants set for signs and seasons, and taking the servant for the Master is the oldest lie there is.
note: 80:1 quote was invented; the live 80:4, 80:6 and 80:7 carry the thought, 80:7 saying outright that men take the stars for gods. Canon kept. Title adjusted to the live words.

title: The years shortened and the order altered — the enemy thinks to change times and laws
summary_md: The deepest corruption in Enoch's vision is not famine or sword but violence done to the reckoning itself: *And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, And their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, And all things on the earth shall alter, And shall not appear in their time: And the rain shall be kept back And the heaven shall withhold (it).* (1 Enoch 80:2). The lights are dragged into it, *And many chiefs of the stars shall transgress the order (prescribed). And these shall alter their orbits and tasks, And not appear at the seasons prescribed to them.* (1 Enoch 80:6), and Enoch had already said where the fault would sit when the count went wrong: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5). This is the little horn's signature in Daniel's night vision: *And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.* (Daniel 7:25). The enemy's aim is the appointed times themselves. If he can shorten the year and shift the order of the stations, the feasts drift and the people keep the wrong days. Isaiah shows the cost when a people lets the ordinance be moved: *The earth also is defiled under the inhabitants thereof; because they have transgressed the laws, changed the ordinance, broken the everlasting covenant.* (Isaiah 24:5). The Creator wrote the reckoning into the lights, *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), so to alter the year is to assault creation's own covenant. The Torah is not the curse here; breaking the order is.
note: 80:10-11 do not exist; the live 80:2 ('the years shall be shortened'), 80:6 and 82:5 carry the thought. Canon kept. Title adjusted.

title: Not at their time — the feasts lost when the reckoning is lost
summary_md: When the order is perverted it lands on the appointed times. Uriel says the moon herself will be thrown off, *And the moon shall alter her order, And not appear at her time.* (1 Enoch 80:4), and that the reckoning will be hidden from the very people who need it: *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). The feasts are not human inventions to be set by convenience. They are Yahuah's (God's) own, fixed in their seasons: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.* (Leviticus 23:2), *These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.* (Leviticus 23:4). Those seasons hang on the luminaries the Creator appointed: *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19). Jubilees foretells the same drift and names what Enoch's vision only shows, that losing the three hundred and sixty-four days is what loses the feasts: *For this reason the years will come upon them when they will disturb (the order), and make an abominable (day) the day of testimony, and an unclean day a feast day, and they will confound all the days, the holy with the unclean, and the unclean day with the holy; for they will go wrong as to the months and sabbaths and feasts and jubilees. For this reason I command and testify to you that you may testify to them; for after your death your children will disturb (them), so that they will not make the year three hundred and sixty-four days only, and for this reason they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh.* (Jubilees 6:37). The Creator's reckoning of whole solar days is the standard, and to lose it is to lose His feasts.
note: 80:12 ('err as to the new moons, sabbaths, festivals, jubilees') is not in Charles — those words are Jubilees 6:37, which the summary already quoted. Re-formed on the live 80:4 and 80:7 with Jubilees carrying the feast list. Title adjusted since the live Enoch verse does not name the feasts.

title: The fruits withheld and evil multiplied — the ground answers a broken order
summary_md: When the order is perverted, the ground itself answers: *And in those times the fruits of the earth shall be backward, And shall not grow in their time, And the fruits of the trees shall be withheld in their time.* (1 Enoch 80:3). The rain goes with the fruit, *And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, And their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, And all things on the earth shall alter, And shall not appear in their time: And the rain shall be kept back And the heaven shall withhold (it).* (1 Enoch 80:2), and the chapter ends in judgment: *And evil shall be multiplied upon them, And punishment shall come upon them So as to destroy all.’* (1 Enoch 80:8). This is covenant cause and effect. Defile the everlasting covenant and the earth withers: *The earth mourneth and fadeth away, the world languisheth and fadeth away, the haughty people of the earth do languish.* (Isaiah 24:4). The drought and the famine are not arbitrary. The same hand that set the lights for the harvest seasons withholds the increase when men forsake His reckoning, and the remedy is never to abandon the order but to return to it.
note: 80:6 'consumed by the sword' is invented; the live 80:2, 80:3 and 80:8 carry the withheld fruit and the judgment. Isaiah 24:4 kept; the sword sentence dropped with the quote. Title adjusted.

title: Declare everything to thy son — the tablets read and handed down
summary_md: Having read the heavenly tablets, Enoch is sent home with a commission to teach: *And those seven holy ones brought me and placed me on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me: ‘Declare everything to thy son Methuselah, and show to all thy children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), for He is their Creator.* (1 Enoch 81:5). He is given one year to do it: *One year we will leave thee with thy son, till thou givest thy (last) commands, that thou mayst teach thy children and record (it) for them, and testify to all thy children; and in the second year they shall take thee from their midst.* (1 Enoch 81:6). He kept the charge, and the next chapter opens with him doing it: *And now, my son Methuselah, all these things I am recounting to thee and writing down for thee, and I have revealed to thee everything, and given thee books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from thy father’s hand, and (see) that thou deliver them to the generations of the world.* (1 Enoch 82:1). This is the Shema's own charge to pass the way down the generations: *And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:* (Deuteronomy 6:6); *And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.* (Deuteronomy 6:7). The Psalm says why the handing down matters, *That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children:* (Psalms 78:6), and the wisdom books say where the writing finally has to land: *Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:* (Proverbs 3:3). The way is kept by being handed down, not invented.
note: Both Enoch quotes were invented (the 'scribe of righteousness' call is not in ch. 81); re-formed on the live 81:5-6 and 82:1. Deuteronomy 6:6-7 and Proverbs 3:3 kept; Psalm 78:6 added from the verse index. Title adjusted.

title: The righteous with the righteous, the apostate with the apostate — the year of testimony
summary_md: Before Enoch is taken, the holy ones tell him how the testimony he leaves will divide the generations after him: *Let thy heart be strong, For the good shall announce righteousness to the good; The righteous with the righteous shall rejoice, And shall offer congratulation to one another.* (1 Enoch 81:7), *But the sinners shall die with the sinners, And the apostate go down with the apostate.* (1 Enoch 81:8). And they warn him that in the meantime the righteous will suffer for what others do: *And those who practise righteousness shall die on account of the deeds of men, And be taken away on account of the doings of the godless.’* (1 Enoch 81:9). This is the first Psalm's two ways laid out before a single generation has walked them: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalm 1:1), *For Yahuah (LORD) knows the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). The reckoning Enoch was about to hand to Methuselah is what the next chapter says the sinners will refuse: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5). So the sorting is by the way a man walks and not by the house he was born in, and the one who keeps what Enoch wrote down walks with the righteous. The commandments were written to be kept, not altered, and the generation that forgets them goes down together.
note: 81:6-7 ('perverse generation... alter the times') do not exist in ch. 81 — that wording is Jubilees 6:37. The live 81:7-9 carry the righteous-with-the-righteous / sinners-with-sinners sorting; re-formed there with 82:5 for the reckoning. Psalm 1:1 kept, 1:6 added from the index; Daniel 7:25, Genesis 1:14 and the Jubilees quotes dropped as they no longer answer the live verse. New title.

title: Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness — no book of unrighteousness written
summary_md: When Enoch has read the book of all the deeds of mankind, the first thing out of his mouth is a blessing on the one whose record is clean: *And after that I said: ‘Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness and goodness, Concerning whom there is no book of unrighteousness written, And against whom no day of judgement shall be found.’* (1 Enoch 81:4). The chapter closes with Enoch coming home the same way, *And in those days they ceased to speak to me, and I came to my people, blessing Yahuah (Lord) of the world.* (1 Enoch 81:10), and the blessing is spelled out in the next chapter for those who keep the reckoning as the sun keeps it: *Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days.* (1 Enoch 82:4). To walk in the reckoning is to keep the appointed times by the lights, the feasts that belong to the Creator and not to men: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.* (Leviticus 23:2). This is the two-ways blessing of the first Psalm: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalm 1:1). And the voice John heard says the same thing Enoch said over the tablets: *And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, says the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.* (Revelation 14:13). The blessing is on the walk, written in a book, and it ain't new.
note: All four Enoch quotes were invented; the live 81:4 ('Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness'), 81:10 and 82:4 carry the blessing. Leviticus 23:2 and Psalm 1:1 kept; Revelation 14:13 added from the index. Title adjusted.

title: Men at fault in the reckoning — the four days they refuse to count
summary_md: Enoch names exactly where the reckoning goes wrong in the hands of men: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5). The four days men drop are not optional; they are part of the year as the Creator counts it: *For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded (thereon) for ever, one in the first portal and one in the third, and one in the fourth and one in the sixth, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.* (1 Enoch 82:6). Uriel had shown Enoch what that fault grows into in the days of the sinners, when the very stars are made to look as if they had changed: *And many chiefs of the stars shall transgress the order (prescribed). And these shall alter their orbits and tasks, And not appear at the seasons prescribed to them.* (1 Enoch 80:6). This is the same enemy Daniel names, the horn that *shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time* (Daniel 7:25). The lights were never men's to alter: *Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), and *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down* (Psalm 104:19). To bow to the host of heaven instead of reading the order their Maker set is the idolatry the Torah forbade: *And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven* (Deuteronomy 4:19). Jubilees names the same falling away from the reckoning: *they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh* (Jubilees 6:37). The times and the laws stand; only the sinners think to change them.
note: The 82:3 quote was invented (its wording is Jubilees 6:37, already quoted); re-formed on the live 82:5-6 and 80:6. Canon and Jubilees kept. Title adjusted.

title: Blessed are all the righteous who walk in the reckoning of their days
summary_md: Against the perversion of the count stands a blessing on those who hold the order: *Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days.* (1 Enoch 82:4). Enoch says the wisdom that carries this reckoning is sweeter than food to the ones who take it in: *And those who understand it shall not sleep, But shall listen with the ear that they may learn this wisdom, And it shall please those that eat thereof better than good food.* (1 Enoch 82:3). This is the blessing of the first Psalm, hung on the man whose reckoning is the Creator's: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful* (Psalm 1:1), *But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night* (Psalm 1:2). The days are reckoned by the sun because the appointed times are the Creator's own appointments and not man's: *These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons* (Leviticus 23:4). To walk in the reckoning is to keep the feasts in their seasons. The Torah stands, and the keeping of it is covenant blessing and never a curse.
note: Both Enoch quotes were invented; the live 82:4 and 82:3 carry the blessing on the reckoning. Psalm 1:1-2 and Leviticus 23:4 kept. Title adjusted to the live words.

title: The reckoning recorded for ever — the luminaries, months and festivals shown by Uriel
summary_md: Enoch hands Methuselah an order that was recorded in heaven before any man counted a day: *For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded (thereon) for ever, one in the first portal and one in the third, and one in the fourth and one in the sixth, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.* (1 Enoch 82:6). He is careful to say where the account came from and who stands over the lights: *And the account thereof is accurate and the recorded reckoning thereof exact; for the luminaries, and months and festivals, and years and days, has Uriel shown and revealed to me, to whom Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the world hath subjected the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 82:7). The lights keep their law because their Maker set them to it: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down* (Psalm 104:19). Jubilees writes the same fixed measure onto the heavenly tables and binds Yashar'el (Israel) to it: *And command you the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they observe the years according to this reckoning-three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts...* (Jubilees 6:32). The year of three hundred and sixty-four whole days is the Creator's covenant order. Man preserves it; he does not author it.
note: Both Enoch quotes were invented; the live 82:6-7 (the anchor span) carry the recorded reckoning and Uriel over the host. Canon and Jubilees kept. Title adjusted.

title: The leaders who watch the seasons and festivals — the four who divide the year
summary_md: Enoch sets out the ranks that govern the year, and he says plainly what they are for: *And these are the orders of the stars, which set in their places, and in their seasons and festivals and months.* (1 Enoch 82:9), *And these are the names of those who lead them, who watch that they enter at their times, in their orders, in their seasons, in their months, in their periods of dominion, and in their positions.* (1 Enoch 82:10). The four who complete the year come first: *Their four leaders who divide the four parts of the year enter first; and after them the twelve leaders of the orders who divide the months; and for the three hundred and sixty (days) there are heads over thousands who divide the days; and for the four intercalary days there are the leaders which sunder the four parts of the year.* (1 Enoch 82:11), and they are named: *And these are the names of the leaders who divide the four parts of the year which are ordained: Mîlkî’êl, Hel’emmêlêk, and Mêl’êjal, and Nârêl.* (1 Enoch 82:13). The seasons and festivals these leaders watch over are exactly what Leviticus names as the Creator's own: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts* (Leviticus 23:2), fixed by the lights of the fourth day: *...and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14). Jubilees ties the same heavenly tables to the feast of weeks as a perpetual renewing of the covenant: *For this reason it is ordained and written on the heavenly tables, that they should celebrate the feast of weeks in this month once a year, to renew the covenant every year...* (Jubilees 6:17). The leaders keep the festivals in their seasons because keeping the appointed times is how the covenant is renewed, and it ain't new.
note: All three Enoch quotes were invented; the live 82:9-11 and 82:13 carry the leaders, seasons and festivals and the four names. Leviticus, Genesis and Jubilees kept.

title: The heaven cast down, the earth swallowed — the deluge foreseen
summary_md: Enoch's first dream-vision is the Flood seen from heaven's side: *And when it fell to the earth I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss, and mountains were suspended on mountains, and hills sank down on hills, and high trees were rent from their stems, and hurled down and sunk in the abyss.* (1 Enoch 83:4). He wakes crying out, and his grandfather tells him what he has seen: *And I recounted to him the whole vision which I had seen, and he said unto me: ‘A terrible thing hast thou seen, my son, and of grave moment is thy dream-vision as to the secrets of all the sin of the earth: it must sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction.* (1 Enoch 83:7). This is Genesis read from above. The sin that brings it is the very violence Yahuah (God) names to Noah: *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence* (Genesis 6:11), so that *Elohim (God) said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth* (Genesis 6:13). The swallowing abyss of the vision is the very mechanism of the deluge, *the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened* (Genesis 7:11), until *every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground... and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark* (Genesis 7:23). Enoch's own book had already carried the word to Noah before the water came: *’Go to Noah and tell him in my name “Hide thyself!” and reveal to him the end that is approaching: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it.* (1 Enoch 10:2). The seed-war of Genesis 6 closes in water, and it ain't new.
note: 83:5 re-pointed to the live 83:4; the 83:7 quote was invented and replaced with the live 83:7 (Mahalalel's reading of the dream). 10:2 stood. Canon kept.

title: The heaven collapsed and fell to the earth — the heavens undone
summary_md: The first thing Enoch sees in the dream is the sky itself coming down: *And regarding them I prayed to Yahuah (Lord). I had laid me down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel, (when) I saw in a vision how the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth.* (1 Enoch 83:3), and the earth under it giving way: *And when it fell to the earth I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss, and mountains were suspended on mountains, and hills sank down on hills, and high trees were rent from their stems, and hurled down and sunk in the abyss.* (1 Enoch 83:4). The prophets and the Revelation see the same unmaking of the heavens on the day of Yahuah (God). Isaiah: *And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree* (Isaiah 34:4). The sixth seal answers it: *And the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together; and every mountain and island were moved out of their places* (Revelation 6:14), and the mountains Enoch saw suspended on mountains are those mountains moved out of their places. Peter binds the flood of water to the coming judgment by fire as one pattern: *Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished* (2 Peter 3:6), so that now *the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment* (2 Peter 3:7). The first dissolution is the picture of the last. The same Word that drowned the old order keeps the present one for the day Enoch's vision foreshadows.
note: 83:10 'rolled up like a scroll' is invented; the live 83:3-4 carry the heaven collapsing and the earth swallowed. Isaiah 34:4, Revelation 6:14 and 2 Peter kept. Title adjusted to the live words.

title: Enoch the intercessor — that a remnant may remain on the earth
summary_md: Mahalalel does not let the dream end in terror. He sends his grandson to pray: *And now, my son, arise and make petition to Yahuah (Lord) of glory, since thou art a believer, that a remnant may remain on the earth, and that He may not destroy the whole earth.* (1 Enoch 83:8), and Enoch does it and writes the prayer down for those who come after: *After that I arose and prayed and implored and besought, and wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world, and I will show everything to thee, my son Methuselah.* (1 Enoch 83:10). The prayer itself asks not for the wicked but for a seed: *And now, O Elohim (God) and Yahuah (Lord) and Great King, I implore and beseech Thee to fulfil my prayer, To leave me a posterity on earth, And not destroy all the flesh of man, And make the earth without inhabitant, So that there should be an eternal destruction.* (1 Enoch 84:5). Enoch stands in the office every true prophet fills afterward, the man who stands in the breach. Abraham bargains the same way before Sodom: *And Abraham drew near, and said, Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?* (Genesis 18:23). Moses turns wrath at Sinai: *Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people* (Exodus 32:12). Amos cries the prophet's plea for the small remnant, *O Yahuah (Lord) GOD, cease, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small* (Amos 7:5), and *Yahuah (LORD) repented for this: This also shall not be* (Amos 7:6). Enoch is the first in that line, and the mercy of the Torah and the standing in the gap of the prophets are already here.
note: The three Enoch quotes were invented; the live 83:8, 83:10 and 84:5 carry the petition for a remnant. Canon kept. Title adjusted.

title: The days of Noah — the Flood as the pattern of the coming judgment
summary_md: Enoch wakes from the vision crying out, *And thereupon a word fell into my mouth, and I lifted up (my voice) to cry aloud, and said: ‘The earth is destroyed.’* (1 Enoch 83:5), and his grandfather tells him it is no idle dream but the sin of the earth coming to its end: *My son, from heaven all this will come upon the earth, and upon the earth there will be great destruction.* (1 Enoch 83:9). That is the Flood set as the pattern for the end, and Yahusha (Jesus) makes the deluge the very figure of His coming: *But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be* (Matthew 24:37), for *they knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be* (Matthew 24:39). The title stands plainly there, the coming of the Son of Adam, the same Son Enoch's own Parables name. Peter draws the same line and presses it toward holiness: *Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness* (2 Peter 3:11). And when the Flood has done its work the covenant mercy turns: *And Elohim (God) remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and Elohim (God) made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged* (Genesis 8:1), the remembering that answers the petition Mahalalel sent Enoch to make, that a remnant might remain. The judgment is real, but it falls on a corrupt and violent generation; the righteous are remembered and kept, and the Torah is never the curse in it.
note: 83:6 quote was invented; the live 83:5 and 83:9 carry Enoch's cry and the destruction from heaven. Matthew 24, 2 Peter 3:11, Genesis 8:1 kept.

title: Thy dominion throughout all generations — the everlasting throne
summary_md: Enoch opens his prayer by exalting the King over a reign that has no end: *‘Blessed be Thou, O Yahuah (Lord), King, Great and mighty in Thy greatness, Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the heaven, King of kings and Elohim (God) of the whole world. And Thy power and kingship and greatness abide for ever and ever, And throughout all generations Thy dominion; And all the heavens are Thy throne for ever, And the whole earth Thy footstool for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 84:2). This is the same confession Nebuchadnezzar is forced to make when his reason returns, *I blessed the El Elyon (most High), and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation* (Daniel 4:34), and *none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou?* (Daniel 4:35). The Psalmist sings the same crown: *Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations.* (Psalm 145:13). Isaiah is shown the throne behind Enoch's words, *I saw also Yahuah (Lord) sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.* (Isaiah 6:1), and the elders at the end echo the everlasting King: *We give thee thanks, O Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.* (Revelation 11:17). The throne Enoch blesses is the same throne the four angels named when they first carried the cry against the Watchers up to heaven: *And they said to Yahuah (Lord) of the ages: ‘Lord of lords, Elohim (God) of gods, King of kings, and Elohim (God) of the ages, the throne of Thy glory (standeth) unto all the generations of the ages, and Thy name holy and glorious and blessed unto all the ages!* (1 Enoch 9:4). The sovereignty is total and ordered and cannot be shaken, and that is the ground on which a remnant can safely be asked for.
note: 84:2 was a paraphrase; replaced with the live 84:2 in full. 9:4 re-quoted from the live text. Canon kept, with the stray single quotes around the canon quotes removed.

title: Nothing hidden from Thee — the eyes on the throne
summary_md: Enoch presses past the throne to the eyes of the One on it: *For Thou hast made and Thou rulest all things, And nothing is too hard for Thee, Wisdom departs not from the place of Thy throne, Nor turns away from Thy presence. And Thou knowest and seest and hearest everything, And there is nothing hidden from Thee [for Thou seest everything].* (1 Enoch 84:3). He is praying in the words the four angels used when they first brought the Watchers' deeds before the throne: *Thou hast made all things, and power over all things hast Thou: and all things are naked and open in Thy sight, and Thou seest all things, and nothing can hide itself from Thee.* (1 Enoch 9:5). Hebrews lifts that line almost word for word into the canon: *Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.* (Hebrews 4:13). David knew there is no hiding from the same gaze, *Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?* (Psalm 139:7), and the same enthroned eyes try the sons of men: *Yahuah (LORD) is in his holy temple, the LORD'S throne is in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men.* (Psalm 11:4). Nothing of the Watchers' secret arts is hidden from Him, which is exactly why Enoch can go on in the next breath to name their trespass and trust the verdict: *And now the angels of Thy heavens are guilty of trespass, And upon the flesh of men abideth Thy wrath until the great day of judgement.* (1 Enoch 84:4).
note: 84:3 was quoted in 9:5's words and 84:8 does not exist; re-formed on the live 84:3 with 9:5 as its echo and 84:4 closing it. Hebrews 4:13, Psalms 139:7 and 11:4 kept. Title adjusted.

title: Leave me a posterity on earth — the plea for a seed and the remnant left
summary_md: Enoch's blessing turns to intercession, and he does not ask for a blanket reprieve. He asks for a seed: *And now, O Elohim (God) and Yahuah (Lord) and Great King, I implore and beseech Thee to fulfil my prayer, To leave me a posterity on earth, And not destroy all the flesh of man, And make the earth without inhabitant, So that there should be an eternal destruction.* (1 Enoch 84:5). Then he asks for the sorting that the Flood will carry out: *And now, my Lord, destroy from the earth the flesh which has aroused Thy wrath, But the flesh of righteousness and uprightness establish as a plant of the eternal seed, And hide not Thy face from the prayer of Thy servant, O Yahuah (Lord).’* (1 Enoch 84:6). The seed preserved through the water is one man and his house: *But Noah found grace in the eyes of Yahuah (LORD).* (Genesis 6:8), so that *Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.* (Genesis 7:23). The plant of the eternal seed Enoch asks for is the remnant the prophets keep coming back to: *Except Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom* (Isaiah 1:9), *yet a remnant of them shall return* (Isaiah 10:22), and Paul reads the same thing in his own day as Yahuah (God) leaving Yashar'el (Israel) a seed: *Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.* (Romans 11:5). The election comes before the preserving. The righteous are already His, and they are the seed left, not a class anyone chooses his way into. Jubilees marks the same lone-survivor mercy, *no man's person was accepted save that of Noah alone... for his heart was righteous in all his ways* (Jubilees 5:19), and Enoch's own commission to Noah had already framed it: *And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.’* (1 Enoch 10:3). The flesh that aroused the wrath is swept off, and the plant of the eternal seed is established, and the two are held together in one prayer.
note: 84:10-12 do not exist; the live 84:5-6 carry the plea for a posterity and the plant of the eternal seed. 10:3 stood. Micah 1:3 and Isaiah 64:1 dropped (they answered the invented 'come forth from Thy habitation' line); the rest of the canon kept. Title adjusted.

title: The black bull gores the red — Cain and Abel, and the seed-war begins
summary_md: Two bulls come forth with the heifer, and the seed-war is drawn at once in their colours: *Before I took thy mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed, and behold a bull came forth from the earth, and that bull was white; and after it came forth a heifer, and along with this (latter) came forth two bulls, one of them black and the other red.* (1 Enoch 85:3), *And that black bull gored the red one and pursued him over the earth, and thereupon I could no longer see that red bull.* (1 Enoch 85:4). The black bull is Cain and the red is Abel slain. The canon tells it plainly: *And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground* (Genesis 4:2), and *Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him* (Genesis 4:8). John reads the very seed-war the colours signal: *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous* (1 John 3:12). That is the line of the wicked one against the righteous line, the tares sown among the wheat from the first field, and Yahusha (Jesus) names that same sowing: *his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat* (Matthew 13:25), *the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one* (Matthew 13:38). Jude marks the apostate by it: *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain* (Jude 1:11). Enoch saw the black bull grow and go on while the red was seen no more, *But that black bull grew and that heifer went with him, and I saw that many oxen proceeded from him which resembled and followed him.’* (1 Enoch 85:5). That is the line of Cain woven in among the white, not the church and not a replacement, but the old seed-war Enoch saw before he ever fathered Methuselah.
note: Draft had the live 85:3 only in part; quoted 85:3 and 85:4 in full and added 85:5 to carry the 'grew' the closing sentence refers to. Canon kept.

title: Enoch taken up to the tower to behold the end
summary_md: When the beasts begin to gore and devour one another, help comes down from heaven: *And I raised mine eyes again to heaven, and I saw in the vision, and behold there came forth from heaven beings who were like white men: and four went forth from that place and three with them.* (1 Enoch 87:2). Three of them take Enoch from among men and set him on a height to watch: *And those three that had last come forth grasped me by my hand and took me up, away from the generations of the earth, and raised me up to a lofty place, and showed me a tower raised high above the earth, and all the hills were lower.* (1 Enoch 87:3), and the charge is given: *And one said unto me: ‘Remain here till thou seest everything that befalls those elephants, camels, and asses, and the stars and the oxen, and all of them.’* (1 Enoch 87:4). This is the same Enoch the canon records was carried off from the generations of the earth: *And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him.* (Genesis 5:24). He is set above to see the whole history play out in figures, the giants born of the stars, the fallen stars themselves, and the oxen of the patriarchal line, whose origin he had already been told: *And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them, That the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.* (Genesis 6:2). The seed-war Enoch is lifted up to watch begins in Genesis 6, runs through the goring beasts, and ends only at the binding the white ones have come down to carry out.
note: 87:5 does not exist (the giants' spirits line); dropped and 87:2 added so the white ones are introduced. 87:3-4 quoted from the live text exactly. Genesis 5:24 and 6:2 kept.
